title: Longest Mirror From a Bag of Letters
statement:
You get a string s of upper- and lowercase English letters. Treat it as a bag of letter tiles. Using some of the tiles, in any order, build the longest possible palindrome: a word that reads the same forwards and backwards.

Return its length. Case matters: "A" and "a" are different tiles.

examples.why: All tiles fit: "abcbcba" uses the pairs of a, b and c, and the leftover b sits in the middle.
Each letter has an odd count. Only one odd tile can sit in the middle, so two of the three leftovers are wasted: 9 − 2.
Different case means different tiles, so there is no pair. Any single tile is a palindrome.

constraints: s contains only English letters, upper and lower case
hints: In a palindrome, every letter except possibly one in the middle appears in matching pairs.
From a letter with count c you can use c if it is even and c − 1 if it is odd.
Add up the even parts, then add 1 if any letter had an odd count: that one tile can go in the middle.

explain.intuition:
A palindrome is a mirror: each tile on the left has a twin on the right. The only exception is the one centre position of an odd-length palindrome. So the order of the input does not matter at all, only the counts.

From each letter take as many full pairs as you can: c tiles if c is even, c − 1 if odd. If at least one letter had a tile left over, place one of them in the middle for a final +1. Only one leftover can be used, however many letters have them.
steps: If any count was odd, add 1.
pitfalls: Adding every odd count in full. Only one odd group can contribute its middle tile; "aaabbbccc" gives 7, not 9.
Skipping odd counts entirely. Three a's still give a pair; only one a is left over.
Folding upper and lower case together. "Aa" has no pair.

solutions.title: Count, take pairs, add a centre
solutions.idea: Sum the even part of every letter count and add one centre tile if any count is odd.

solutions.title: Match pairs on the fly
solutions.idea: Keep a set of letters waiting for a partner. A second copy completes a pair (+2) and leaves the set. At the end, if anything is still waiting, one of them takes the centre.

followups: Return one longest palindrome, not just its length. If several exist, return the alphabetically smallest.
The tiles are now whole words, and a palindrome is built from words (like "ab" + "ba"). How do you pair them?
